accuracy.reason: Gilbert-Lynch definitions/proof, Raft majority behavior, Brewer recovery discussion and DynamoDB read modes support the claims. Overlap ordering, unbounded eventual completion and reconciliation limits are precise.

evidence.quote: Overlapping operations may be placed in either order, provided the resulting order is valid for one copy.

mechanisms.reason: Every card objective is causally supported. The 10-to-12 partition trace exposes missing information, guessing is ruled out, CP/AP behaviors and recovery consequences follow. Diagrams accurately show isolated knowledge and a qualified majority protocol.

evidence.quote: Guessing the new value cannot guarantee correctness across possible unseen writes.

coherence.reason: Distributed communication precedes each guarantee, then the impossibility trace, alternative behaviors, convergence and operation-level choice. Introduced definitions are reused rather than assuming outside knowledge.

evidence.quote: The obstacle is missing information, not a particular database product.

decisions.reason: Strict and stale-tolerant operations have explicit user-visible waits/failure or old data; conflict-resolution and lost-intent costs are explicit. CAP is separated from normal latency/cost decisions.

evidence.quote: Selecting one conflicting value can lose another user's intent, and cross-record rules require their own protection.

clarity.reason: Precise terms are immediately explained, small examples clarify the impossibility and selective design consequences, and no unnecessary recurring story is imposed.

evidence.quote: The theorem requires eventual per-request completion and sets no practical response-time target.

outcomes.reason: All six criteria satisfied: actual learner explains networked copies, conditional limit, live-but-separated nodes, partition tolerance and why ignoring communication failures does not remove them.

All six criteria satisfied: real-time single-copy ordering including overlap, later-read rule, distinction from ACID/eventual convergence, eventual per-request completion without latency bound, refusal/error failure and uptime distinction. Exact quotes entail reasoning.

All three criteria satisfied: learner correctly transfers 10/12 teaching to 0/1, identifies B knowledge and required read, and rejects stale return, indefinite refusal and lucky guessing as simultaneous guarantees.

All six criteria satisfied: safe-order restrictions and affected waits, continued majority operations, local old reads, conflicting accepted writes, explicit reconciliation and lack of automatic intent/business-rule preservation.

All six criteria satisfied: conditional convergence, no deadline/read-your-writes promise, policy-defined surviving intent, strict versus stale-tolerant operation behavior during and after split, and operation-specific guarantees separated from normal latency/cost.

sourceChecks.claim: Gilbert-Lynch theorem verifies impossibility of atomic consistency plus availability when messages can be lost.
Gilbert-Lynch partition model permits messages between components to be lost while nodes continue executing.
Gilbert-Lynch atomic data-object definition verifies total order respecting completed-write/later-read relationships; overlap ordering is the corresponding linearizability consequence.
Gilbert-Lynch availability definition requires eventual termination for every request at non-failing nodes with no response-time bound; refusal is not a successful read.
Gilbert-Lynch proof partitions two sets, completes a write in one and later reads in the other; missing information prevents guaranteed correct response.
Raft paper section 2 verifies safety through partitions and functionality for a communicating majority; supports qualified two-of-three example.
Brewer authored CAP retrospective verifies operation-level partition choices and explicit recovery/reconciliation, including invariant repair.
DynamoDB read-consistency page verifies eventual reads can miss recent writes and distinct operation read modes; Brewer reconciliation discussion supplies convergence and conflict-policy limits.
Brewer retrospective explicitly rejects universal two-of-three framing and permits choices per operation/data; CAP does not itself calculate normal latency or cost.
